hypothesis: H-UNQ-1 blind stepover-radiometric conduit dots: place sparse soft dots on off-catalogue USGS SGMC geologic-map faults (>300 m from the mapped catalogue, dilated 1 px), boosted where GeoDAWN radiometric K/TC anomaly is high, corroborated by GDR 1391 geothermal wells/springs (temperature-weighted) and Quaternary vents, slight LiDAR-scarp context, distance penalty to TIGER roads (road edges mimic scarps); zeroed exactly on the mapped catalogue; non-maximum suppressed at >= 2 px; capped at 34,000 dots (champion budget class). Targets hidden faults missing from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue rather than re-dotting the D2.x family every champion reuses.
mechanism: DTI (alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300 m triangular kernel) rewards predictions within 300 m of truth and penalizes false-positive mass. Champion scores (0.26-0.2778 owner-reported) came from sparsifying one nested dotted support (H19-5 121,131 px -> D2.8 44,090 px -> B=1 40,199 px -> B=2 37,654 px = h33-2-b2), which cuts redundant FP mass. H-UNQ-1 keeps the sparse-dot FP control but moves the nuclei off-catalogue onto blind-structure evidence, so it captures truth pixels the dotted family cannot reach while staying below the 70%/0.90 duplication thresholds.
named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts, mafic dikes, shoreline/terrace risers, road edges and magnetic flight-line artifacts can all look like fault or alteration signatures. Mitigations: require off-catalogue SGMC-trace nuclei, concurrence with radiometric K/TC anomaly, well/vent corroboration, and a road-distance penalty; none of these remove the mimic risk entirely.
